market._comment: St. John's, Newfoundland — NOT South Florida. Earlier versions of this system inherited 'South Florida' from a placeholder in the original design brief and repeated it in every agent prompt; it was wrong. The Meta ad account bills in CAD, which is consistent with this.

outcomeStages._comment: This team does NOT use GHL's won/lost status — every opportunity sits at status 'open' and the outcome is signalled by dragging the card to a terminal column. Reading status alone returned null for all 149 leads, zeroing revenue and making the ROAS rule unfireable. These stage names are how won/lost is actually determined. 'Buyer Confirmed' and 'Listing Active' are NOT included as won — both carry deal values but are arguably mid-pipeline, so Jacob should confirm before counting them as revenue.
outcomeStages.activeStagesNote: Jacob, 2026-08-24: these are NOT won, but they ARE active pipeline value. Verified against the live DB on that date: Buyer Confirmed = 9 deals / $21,450.00, Listing Active = 1 deal / $4,048.50, so pipeline value is $25,498.50 against $11,247.00 of banked revenue (2 deals at Deal Closed). They stay won=null, so revenue and ROAS are untouched; they are totalled separately as pipeline_value. Counting them as won would have overstated revenue as $36,745.50 on deals that have not closed. UPDATED 2026-08-25: 'Seller Confirmed' added. Mark's pipeline mapping showed it as an under-contract stage alongside 'Buyer Confirmed' — a formally signed seller. I had missed it because it carried no deal value at the time I checked the data, so it never surfaced. Same commitment level as the other two; it belongs here.

ghl._credentialsNote: Live GHL credentials are stored in the database (ghl_credentials), entered via the dashboard Settings page — not in this file.

meta._comment: Real estate IS a Meta restricted category (HOUSING), unlike Matama. This means no age/gender targeting, no sub-15mi radius, no lookalikes — the compliance gate in shared/meta/compliance.ts enforces this and cannot be overridden. Credentials live in the database, not here.

forge._comment: All values CAD. Grounded in real data pulled 2026-08-24 over a 30-day window: $1,131.37 total spend, $37.71/day actual, 3,203 clicks, $0.35 blended CPC. Client's own Meta daily budget is $50 ($30 buyers / $20 sellers).
forge.cplThresholdNote: UNVALIDATED. Zero leads carry ad attribution yet, so real CPL is unknown — at a 3% click-to-lead rate it would be ~$12, at 1% ~$35. Revisit once attribution produces the first 20-30 leads.
forge.roasNote: Rule DISABLED until revenue data is trustworthy. Only 4 of 149 leads carry a non-zero deal value. A rule that can never fire is worse than no rule — it looks like coverage that doesn't exist. Re-enable once outcomeStages above are confirmed and deal values are being recorded consistently.
forge.dailyBudgetCapNote: Was 500 — ten times the client's actual $50/day budget, so it was no guardrail at all. 75 allows 50% headroom to scale while still catching a runaway.
forge.fatigueThresholdNote: Was 0.7, which is mathematically impossible to stay under: frequency is impressions/reach, so any running ad is >= 1. All 63 ad sets exceeded it, meaning it would have flagged everything as fatigued forever. Their actual range is 1.48 avg / 1.88 max, so 3.0 sits above normal operation but still catches genuine fatigue.

qualificationQuestions: Are you looking to buy or sell?
What area are you interested in?
Are you pre-approved? What's your budget range?

writeFields._comment: Iris build-brief update, 2026-08-25: Iris must write structured fields after a call, never prose into isa_notes — that field only needs a parser (agents/scout/isa-notes.ts) because the ISA's answers are trapped in prose, and Iris repeating that pattern would automate the bottleneck instead of fixing it. These are single write-target keys, not scout.fields' read-priority lists: scout.fields.timeline tries the survey field first because that is what is populated when a lead arrives; Iris writes to the LF field specifically, because that is the one the ISA has historically written after a call.
writeFields.preApprovedNote: Written as the actual financing value — cash / pre-approved / in-progress / not-approved — not a yes/no. See agents/scout/isa-notes.ts Financing type.

callbacks._comment: Mark, 2026-09-03: no GHL calendar involved here anymore. When a lead asks to be called back at a specific time, Iris writes a note (notesFieldKey below) and the system itself re-dials at that time — see agents/iris/dial-pending.ts's is_explicit_callback and webhooks/vapi-tools.ts's handleScheduleCallback. Superseded the GHL-calendar-booking design below the fold on 2026-09-02, which is on hold, not deleted — see calendarNote.
callbacks.notesFieldKeyNote: Same underlying field as scout.fields.isaNotes below, but named separately here as a single write target (not a read-priority list) — see IrisConfig.callbackNotesFieldKey.
callbacks.calendarNote: 3% REC - ISA Callback (Iris), id buxIQTE3TkpVpjrYBaRc, still exists in GHL (currently inactive) from the earlier calendar-booking design. Nothing in code reads it anymore — left as-is rather than deleted in case the calendar-booking approach comes back.

outreachCadence._comment: Jacob, 2026-08-25: Iris calls new leads morning and afternoon for the first 3-4 days trying to reach them. Iris owns this cadence internally — Scout fires ONCE per lead and does not trigger per attempt. scout.touchedTags gates whether a sequence STARTS, not each call.
outreachCadence.recheckReason: The human ISA is on until the end of the month, so both they and Iris may work the same lead. Iris must re-check the contact before EVERY attempt, not just at sequence start, or a lead the ISA already spoke to on day 2 keeps getting called on days 3 and 4.

transferNumbers._comment: Mark, 2026-09-02: two ring-group numbers, one per intent — every agent under the number rings simultaneously, first pickup wins, ringing stops for everyone else. Used for Vapi's live-transfer tool; separate from scout.calendars (buyer/seller consultation booking) and callbacks.calendarIds (the ISA quick-callback fallback, also buyer/seller) above.

scout._comment: Lead intake mapping for 3% East Coast, from Mark's GHL discovery (2026-08-25), verified against the live location before being committed. Every stage ID he mapped resolved correctly. Two values were corrected — see _corrections.

_corrections.preApprovedField: Mark had contact.are_you_pre_approved. No such field exists. The real key is contact.are_you_pre_approuved — GHL's own label carries a typo ('Are You Pre-approuved ?'). This mattered: Mark notes pre-approval is the ONLY real scoring signal the ISA uses, and a wrong key returns null rather than erroring, so every lead would have silently read as not-pre-approved.
_corrections.buyerCalendarId: Mark had 4Eyz51DOl7TY78gRgBU3 (lowercase L at index 8); the real ID is 4Eyz51DOI7TY78gRgBU3 (uppercase i). Same length, one glyph apart — transcribed by eye. Every buyer booking would have failed. The seller calendar was correct.
_corrections.leadSourceNote: Mark noted 'no custom source/campaign field exists'. That was true when he looked but is now out of date: nine attribution fields (fbclid, utm_*, meta_campaign/adset/ad_id) were provisioned into this location. Scout reads those for ad-level attribution and falls back to the built-in contact.source only when they are empty.

intakeStages._comment: No single 'new' stage — the lead type IS the entry stage. Lead type is also captured in the propertyInterest field.

scout.qualifiedTagsNote: Qualification is not a pipeline stage — the ISA qualifies and books or transfers on the same call, so any of these tags means qualified. Two corrections to Mark's original pair: 'appointment' (16 contacts) means the same thing as 'appt booked' (60), and 'live transfered' with one r exists on 8 contacts against 5 for the correct spelling. Matching only the correct spelling missed 8 of 13 live transfers — 62%. Jacob confirms only the correct spelling is used now, but the misspelling is kept because the historical records still carry it and tag text drifts.

calendars._comment: buyer/seller are the client's consultation calendars. 'callback' is a separate calendar used ONLY by Iris, for when a lead asks to be called back at a specific time — kept apart from the consultation calendars so a callback is never mistaken for a booked appointment, and so the team can see Iris's commitments in GHL rather than them living only inside our system. Empty until created; see iris.callbacks.

fields._comment: Each entry is tried in order. Survey fields come FIRST because they are the only ones populated when a lead arrives — measured across 49 contacts that had never been called, the LF fields were empty on all of them while the survey fields were present on 25-30. Mark's original mapping had this inverted: it treated what_is_your_budget and when_are_you_looking_to_move as stale duplicates 'not used going forward' and pointed at the LF fields instead. In fact what_is_your_budget is populated on 90 of 150 contacts against lf_budget's 12, and the LF fields are written by the ISA after a call, not by the form. The LF entries are kept as second choice since the ISA does still fill them in.

_liveDataFindings.checkedOn: 2026-08-25, against 80 contacts and 222 opportunities in the live location
_liveDataFindings.propertyInterestNeverPopulated: contact.lf_proprety is EMPTY on all 80 contacts checked. The field exists and the key is correct, it is simply never written. Intent is therefore derived from the intake stage the lead lands in (Buyer/Seller/Downsize/Upgrading Leads), not from this field.
_liveDataFindings.preApprovedNeverPopulated: contact.are_you_pre_approuved is empty on all 150 contacts checked — the ISA never fills the form field in. It is captured in the free-text ISA NOTES field instead ('Pre-approved: yes', 'Pre-approved: paying cash', 'Pre-approved: no, in the process'). Scout parses that; see agents/scout/isa-notes.ts. The dedicated field is still read first in case the team starts using it.
_liveDataFindings.timelineValues: contact.lf_timeframe is populated on 21/80 and holds '1-4 Months' (most common), '4+ months', 'ASAP', and '1 - 4 months'. Spacing is inconsistent because the form has been revised.
_liveDataFindings.intakeStagesAreTransient: Only 1 of 222 opportunities sits in an intake stage — leads move through quickly. Intent resolution therefore works at capture time, which is when Scout runs, and reads 'unknown' for the existing back catalogue. Expected, not a fault.
_liveDataFindings.noAdAttributionYet: 0 of 60 contacts carry fbclid or meta_ad_id. The fields exist; nothing is populating them until the landing page and Meta ad set URL parameters pass them through.
_liveDataFindings.isaNotesIsTheRealSource: ISA NOTES is populated on 101 of 150 contacts and carries more usable signal than any dedicated field. Reading it lifted financing from 0 to 16 records, timeline from 21 to 62 and budget to 49, and took leads carrying any score from a handful to 135 of 150. Two note formats exist: buyers get Area/1st Time Buyer/Price Range/Pre-approved/When, sellers get area/reason/timeline.
_liveDataFindings.cashBuyersAreNotFailedApprovals: Five contacts answered 'paying cash', 'cash', 'no need' or 'not necessary'. Three of those begin with a negation but describe the strongest possible buyer — no lender, no appraisal, no financing condition. A boolean pre-approved flag would have scored them as negatives, so financing is modelled as cash | pre-approved | in-progress | not-approved | null and cash scores highest.
_liveDataFindings.surveyFieldsAreTheIntakeData: Corrects the earlier note that nothing is available at lead arrival. Survey answers DO come in with the lead: when_are_you_looking_to_move (113/150 overall, 30/49 on never-called contacts), what_is_your_budget (90/150), are_you_currently_working_with_a_realtor (90/150). The LF fields and ISA notes are post-call. So intake scoring is viable on timeline and budget; financing is not, because it only ever appears after a call.
_liveDataFindings.realtorFieldHasNoVariance: are_you_currently_working_with_a_realtor is 'No' on all 90 contacts that answer it. Captured for context but deliberately NOT scored — a field with one value carries no information, and scoring it would inflate every lead equally while looking like a real signal. Worth revisiting if a 'Yes' ever appears, which would be a strong negative.
_liveDataFindings.timelineScoredNumerically: Timeline is parsed to a month count rather than matched as text. Two string-matching versions were wrong: the first scored '1-4 Months' at zero, the second scored the survey values '3-6 Months', '4 - 6 months', '7 - 12 months' and '12 + months' at zero — 32 of 113 real answers. The two sources use different formats and the forms keep being revised, so patterns rot; a number does not.
_liveDataFindings.freshLeadCoverage: Corrects an earlier, looser measurement. Using 'no ISA notes' as a proxy for 'never contacted' was wrong — it included leads the text automation had already worked (21 of 49 carried 'replied'). On strictly fresh leads (buyer/seller tag, no ISA notes, no touch tags) the survey data is near-complete: timeline 9/9, budget 8/9, all scoring above zero. Only 9 such leads in a 150-contact sample, so treat as directional.

scout.newLeadTagsNote: Applied automatically by the form workflow when a lead is created (confirmed by Jacob 2026-08-25). These are Scout's intake trigger. 14 of 150 contacts carry no tags at all; per Jacob only leads in the pipeline matter and those are all tagged, so untagged contacts are out of scope rather than a gap in coverage.
scout.touchedTagsNote: Evidence that a lead has actually been SPOKEN TO, so Iris should not open a new outreach sequence. 'replied' was originally in this list and has been removed: it is applied when a lead answers the text automation, which is engagement, not a conversation. 10 of 150 contacts carry 'replied' with no other contact evidence — they answered a text and nobody ever called them. Those are among the hottest leads on the board and blocking them was exactly backwards. Note this gates whether Iris STARTS a sequence, not each call within it: Iris dials morning and afternoon for 3-4 days and owns that cadence itself.
